scope: Derived analysis of existing saved HTTP probe summaries and Server logs; no new runtime, test, HTTP request, or credential scan.
validation: All logged telemetry prefix records parsed as JSON, with fixed fields matching PerformanceEvent; version, UTC timestamp, enums, identifiers, numeric types/ranges, script entry shape and bounded length checked.
Frame records have Frames=1 and MaxWallMs=WallMs; mode detail setting, drain format, accepted totals and presence per logged PID checked.
Detailed run frame events equal summary completed frames per logged PID; this observation applies only to this finite run.
limitations: Worker telemetry is logged as untrusted stderr; authors can forge records, so these observations are not a security audit.

Worker Dropped covers Worker-side collection, detail and sink losses; Hosting drain invalid, oversized, rateDropped and queueDropped are separate counters. Zero observed counters do not prove delivery in other executions.

Two active heartbeats were observed in the summary run; none were observed in the detailed run. Heartbeats cover already-started frame slots and do not establish coverage of initialization, gate waits, or full HTTP requests.
Phase timings are inclusive; ScriptMs may overlap PrepareMs. Frame wall excludes session gate wait and input validation and is not HTTP latency.
Worker collector and Hosting drain shutdown are bounded and best effort; emitted observations are not proof that every possible event was retained.
This finite local HTTP/Worker evidence does not establish performance targets, GPU hardware timing or VRAM, cross-platform or browser behavior.
The earlier http-summary-final1 run failed due to an Oracle/Worker binary mismatch and is excluded from the passed runs.
HTTP counts and credential scan counts are transcribed from probe summary files; this audit did not independently replay HTTP or rescan files.
